source_text: Ὁ δεῖνα περίβλεπτος ἐπὶ χρημάτων περιουσίᾳ· καὶ πλῆθος περὶ αὐτὸν κολάκων· δορυφορία φίλων προσποιητῶν τὴν ἀπ' αὐτοῦ χάριν θεραπευόντων· πλῆθος συγγενείας, καὶ ταύτης κατεσχημα τισμένης· ἑσμὸς τῶν ἐφεπομένων μυρίος τῶν τε ἐπὶ σιτίων καὶ τῶν κατὰ τὰς χρείας αὐτῷ προσεδρευόντων, οὓς καὶ προϊὼν καὶ πάλιν ἐπανιὼν ἐπισυρόμενος ἐπίφθονός ἐστι τοῖς ἐντυγχάνουσι. Πρόσθες τῷ πλούτῳ καὶ πολιτικήν τινα δυναστείαν, ἢ καὶ τὰς ἐκ βασιλέων τιμάς· ἢ ἐθνῶν ἐπιμέλειαν· ἢ στρατοπέδων ἡγεμονίαν· τὸν κήρυκα μέγα βοῶντα πρὸ αὐτοῦ· τοὺς ῥαβδούχους ἔνθεν καὶ ἔνθεν βαρυ τάτην κατάπληξιν τοῖς ἀρχομένοις ἐμβάλλοντας τὰς πληγάς· τὰς δημεύσεις· τὰς ἀπαγωγάς· τὰ δεσμωτήρια, ἐξ ὧν ἀφόρητος ὁ παρὰ τῶν ὑποχειρίων συναθροίζεται φόβος. Καὶ τί μετὰ τοῦτο; Μία νὺξ, ἢ πυρετὸς εἷς, ἢ πλευρῖτις, ἢ περιπνευμονία, ἀνάρπαστον ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ἀπάγουσα τὸν ἄνθρωπον οἴχεται, πᾶσαν τὴν κατ' αὐτὸν σκηνὴν ἐξαπίνης ἀπογυμνώσασα, καὶ ἡ δόξα ἐκείνη ὥσπερ ἐνύπνιον ἀπηλέγχθη. Ὥστε ἐπιτέτευκται τῷ προφήτῃ ἡ πρὸς τὸ ἀδρανέστατον ἄνθος ὁμοίωσις τῆς ἀνθρωπίνης δόξης. 5.3 Βλαστησάτω ἡ γῆ βοτάνην χόρτου, σπεῖρον σπέρμα κατὰ γένος καὶ καθ' ὁμοιότητα. Ἔτι καὶ νῦν ἡ τάξις τῶν φυομένων μαρτυρεῖ τῇ πρώτῃ διακοσμήσει. Ἡ γὰρ βλάστησις καθηγεῖται πάσης βοτάνης καὶ πάσης πόας. Εἴτε γὰρ ἀπὸ ῥίζης ἐκδίδοταί τι ἐκ τῆς κάτωθεν προβολῆς, ὡς κρόκος καὶ ἄγρωστις, ἀναβλαστῆσαι δεῖ καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ ἔξω προκύψαι· εἴτε ἀπὸ σπέρματος, καὶ οὕτως ἀνάγκη πρῶτον βλάστησιν, εἶτα βοτάνην γενέσθαι, εἶτα χόρτον χλοάζοντα, εἶτα τὸν καρπὸν ἐπὶ ξηρᾶς ἤδη καὶ παχείας τῆς καλάμης ἁδρυνόμενον. Βλαστησάτω ἡ γῆ βοτάνην χόρτου. Ὅταν εἰς γῆν καταπέσῃ τὸ σπέρμα συμμέτρως νοτίδος καὶ θέρμης ἔχουσαν, χαῦνον γενόμενον καὶ πολύπορον, τῆς παρακειμένης γῆς περιδραξάμενον, τὰ οἰκεῖα καὶ σύμφυλα πρὸς ἑαυτὸ ἐπισπᾶται. Ἐμπίπτοντα δὲ τοῖς πόροις καὶ περιολισθαίνοντα τῆς γῆς τὰ λεπτότατα μόρια, ἐπὶ πλέον ἀνευρύνει τοὺς ὄγκους αὐτῆς ὥστε ῥιζοῦσθαι μὲν εἰς τὸ κάτω, ἐπὶ τὸ ἄνω δὲ προκύπτειν ἰσαρίθμων ταῖς ῥίζαις τῶν καλάμων προβαλλομένων· θαλπομένου δὲ ἀεὶ τοῦ βλαστήματος, συρομένην διὰ τῶν ῥιζῶν τὴν νοτίδα, τῇ ὁλκῇ τοῦ θερμοῦ συνεπάγεσθαι τοῦ τροφίμου τῆς γῆς ὅσον μέτριον, καὶ τοῦτο καταμερίζειν εἰς καλάμην καὶ φλοιὸν καὶ τὰς θήκας τοῦ σίτου, καὶ αὐτὸν τὸν σῖτον καὶ τοὺς ἀνθέρικας· καὶ οὕτω κατὰ μικρὸν τῆς αὐξήσεως γινομένης, ἐπὶ τὸ οἰκεῖον μέτρον ἕκαστον τῶν φυομένων ἀποκαθίστασθαι, εἴτε τι τῶν σιτηρῶν, εἴτε τῶν χεδροπῶν, εἴτε τῶν λαχανωδῶν ἢ φρυγανικῶν τυγχάνοι. Εἷς χόρτος καὶ μία βοτάνη ἐξαρκεῖ τὴν διάνοιάν σου πᾶσαν εἰς τὴν θεωρίαν τῆς ἐξεργασαμένης αὐτὰ τέχνης ἀπασχολῆσαι· πῶς γόνασι διαζώννυται ἡ καλάμη τοῦ σίτου, ἵνα ὥσπερ σύνδεσμοί τινες ῥᾳδίως τὸ βάρος τῶν ἀσταχύων φέρωσιν, ὅταν πλήρεις ὄντες καρπῶν πρὸς τὴν γῆν κατακλίνωνται. Διὰ τοῦτο ὁ μὲν βρόμος διόλου κενὸς, ἅτε μηδενὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν βαρυνόμενος· τὸν δὲ σῖτον τοῖς συνδέσμοις τούτοις ἡ φύσις κατησφαλίσατο. Ἐν θήκῃ δὲ τὸν κόκκον ἀποθεμένη ὡς μὴ εὐδιάρπαστον εἶναι τοῖς σπερμολόγοις· ἔτι καὶ τῇ προβολῇ τῶν ἀνθερίκων οἷον ἀκίσι τὰς ἐκ τῶν μικρῶν ζῴων ἀφίστησι βλάβας.
thought_title: The fleeting glory of the powerful and the ordered growth of plants
orientation: Basil is preaching on the creation of vegetation, and has just compared human glory to the flower of grass; he now expands that comparison with a portrait of a powerful man, then turns to the literal process by which seeds sprout and grow.
pass_a_gloss: Some man is conspicuous for abundance of wealth; and a crowd of flatterers is around him; a bodyguard of pretended friends who cultivate his favor; a crowd of relatives, and this one too having been arranged; a countless swarm of those following him, both of those attending him for food and of those for his needs, whom both going out and again returning he drags along, and he is envied by those who meet him. Add to the wealth also some political power, or also the honors from kings; or care of nations; or command of armies; the herald crying loudly before him; the rod-bearers on this side and on that side casting a very heavy terror upon the ruled, the blows; the confiscations; the arrests; the prisons, from which an unbearable fear is gathered from those under his hand. And what after this? One night, or one fever, or pleurisy, or pneumonia, carrying off the man snatched away from men, departs, having suddenly stripped bare all the tent around him, and that glory was exposed as a dream. So that the comparison of human glory to the weakest flower has been achieved by the prophet. Let the earth sprout the herb of grass, sowing seed according to kind and according to likeness. Even now the order of the things that grow bears witness to the first arrangement. For the sprouting goes before every herb and every grass. For whether something is given out from a root from the projection below, as crocus and dog's tooth grass, it must sprout up and push out to the outside; or whether from seed, even so it is necessary first that there be sprouting, then that it become herb, then green grass, then the fruit being ripened on the already dry and thick stalk. Let the earth sprout the herb of grass. Whenever the seed falls into earth that has moisture and warmth in due measure, having become porous and with many pores, having grasped the surrounding earth, it draws to itself the things that are akin and of the same kind. And the finest particles of the seed, falling into the pores and slipping through the earth, widen the bulk of the earth more and more, so that it is rooted downward, and upward the stalks are projected equal in number to the roots; and while the sprout is always being warmed, the moisture drawn through the roots is carried along with the drawing of the heat, and a measured amount of the nourishing part of the earth, and this it distributes into stalk and husk and the sheaths of the grain, and the grain itself and the awns; and so, as the growth happens little by little, each of the things that grow is restored to its proper measure, whether it happens to be one of the grain crops, or of the legumes, or of the vegetables or of the brushwood. One grass and one herb is enough to occupy your whole mind for the contemplation of the art that has worked them out; how the stalk of the grain is girded with joints, so that like certain bindings they easily bear the weight of the ears, whenever being full of fruits they are bent down toward the earth. For this reason the wild oat is entirely hollow, since it is weighed down in its head by nothing; but the grain nature has secured with these bindings. And having stored the kernel in a sheath, so that it is not easily snatched away by the seed-pickers; and still by the projection of the awns, as with points, it keeps away the harms from the small animals.

choices.why: δορυφορία is literally a spear-bearing bodyguard; προσποιητῶν means pretended or feigned, so the phrase is deliberately ironic about false friends acting as guards.

choices.english: he is envied by those who meet him
choices.why: ἐπίφθονος means envied or liable to envy; the dative τοῖς ἐντυγχάνουσι marks those who encounter him as the ones feeling envy.
rejected: he is an object of envy to those he meets

choices.why: ἀπελέγχω means to refute or expose as false; Basil says the glory was shown to be no more real than a dream, preserving the passive force.

choices.english: the comparison has been achieved by the prophet
choices.why: ἐπιτυγχάνω in the perfect passive means to have succeeded in or achieved something; Basil says Isaiah's image has hit the mark.
rejected: the likeness has been attained by the prophet
the prophet has succeeded in the comparison

choices.english: the things that are akin and of the same kind
choices.why: οἰκεῖα means proper to itself or akin, and σύμφυλα means of the same kind or tribe; Basil describes the seed drawing to itself what belongs to its own nature.

choices.english: widen the bulk of the earth
choices.why: The subject is the seed's finest particles; they widen the earth's bulk (αὐτῆς refers to γῆς), as the seed's particles penetrate and loosen the surrounding earth.

bible_refs.note: Βλαστησάτω ἡ γῆ βοτάνην χόρτου, σπεῖρον σπέρμα κατὰ γένος καὶ καθ' ὁμοιότητα
Allusion to the earlier quotation: πᾶσα σὰρξ χόρτος, καὶ πᾶσα δόξα ἀνθρώπου ὡς ἄνθος χόρτου

pass_b_english: One man is admired for his abundance of wealth. Around him is a crowd of flatterers, a bodyguard of pretended friends who court his favor, a host of relatives, and these too merely for show. There is a vast swarm of attendants, some for his table and some for his daily needs, whom he drags along as he goes out and comes back, and he is envied by those who meet him. Add to the wealth some political power, or honors from kings, or the governance of nations, or command of armies: the herald shouting loudly before him, the lictors on either side striking blows that fill the governed with the heaviest dread, the confiscations, the arrests, the prisons, from which an unbearable fear is gathered from those under his hand. And what comes after this? One night, or a single fever, or pleurisy, or pneumonia, carries the man off, snatched away from among human beings, and is gone, suddenly stripping bare the whole stage-setting around him, and that glory was confuted like a dream. So the prophet's comparison of human glory to the weakest flower has hit the mark.

"Let the earth sprout the herb of grass, bearing seed according to kind and according to likeness" (Genesis 1:11). Even now the order of growing things testifies to that first arrangement. For sprouting comes first for every herb and every grass. Whether something is sent out from a root by a shoot from below, like the crocus and the dog's-tooth grass, it must first sprout and push out to the surface; or whether it comes from seed, in that case too there must first be sprouting, then the herb, then the green grass, then the fruit ripening on the now dry and thick stalk. "Let the earth sprout the herb of grass." When the seed falls into earth that has a proper measure of moisture and warmth, it becomes porous and full of holes, takes hold of the surrounding earth, and draws to itself the things that are akin and of the same kind. The finest particles of the seed enter the pores of the earth and slip through them, and they widen its own bulk more and more, so that the seed takes root downward and pushes upward, sending out stalks equal in number to the roots. As the sprout is continually warmed, the moisture drawn through the roots brings up with it, by the pull of the heat, a measured amount of the earth's nourishment, and distributes it into stalk and husk and the sheaths of the grain, and into the grain itself and the awns. And so, as the growth proceeds little by little, each of the growing things reaches its proper measure, whether it is one of the grains, or the legumes, or the vegetables, or the brushwood.

One grass and one herb is enough to occupy your whole mind in contemplating the skill that produced them: how the stalk of the grain is girded with joints, so that like some kind of bindings they easily bear the weight of the ears when they are full of fruit and bend down toward the ground. For this reason brome-grass is entirely hollow, since its head is weighed down by nothing; but the grain nature has secured with these bindings. And it has placed the kernel in a sheath so that it is not easily snatched away by seed-pickers; and further, by the projection of the awns, as with points, it keeps off the harm from small creatures.

problems.why: βρόμος means 'oats' as a weed/grain, but context contrasts it with wheat; 'oat' misleads as cultivated grain.

fixed: βρόμος means 'brome-grass', a wild grass, not cultivated oats; the context contrasts it with wheat, so 'brome-grass' is the accurate rendering.

problems.quote: that glory was exposed as a dream
problems.source_quote: ἡ δόξα ἐκείνη ὥσπερ ἐνύπνιον ἀπηλέγχθη
problems.why: ἀπηλέγχθη is passive, 'was refuted/disproved', not 'exposed'; glory was shown false, not merely revealed.
problems.fix: that glory was confuted like a dream

problems.why: κατεσχηματισμένης means 'pretended'/'made up', not 'carefully arranged'; relatives are feigned/ostentatious, not organized.
problems.fix: and these too merely for show
problems.ruling: κατεσχηματισμένης means 'feigned/pretended'; 'carefully arranged' misleads reader about false relatives.

problems.quote: from which an unbearable fear gathers among those under his authority
problems.source_quote: ἐξ ὧν ἀφόρητος ὁ παρὰ τῶν ὑποχειρίων συναθροίζεται φόβος
problems.why: παρὰ τῶν ὑποχειρίων means 'from those under him' (fear coming from the subjects), not 'among those under his authority'.
problems.fix: from which an unbearable fear is gathered from those under his hand
problems.ruling: παρὰ τῶν ὑποχειρίων means 'from those under him'; fear comes FROM subjects, not 'among' them.

problems.quote: sowing seed according to kind and according to likeness
problems.source_quote: σπεῖρον σπέρμα κατὰ γένος καὶ καθ' ὁμοιότητα
problems.why: σπεῖρον is 'bearing seed' (participle of σπείρω), not 'sowing seed'; the herb bears seed, it doesn't sow it.
problems.fix: bearing seed according to kind and according to likeness
problems.ruling: σπεῖρον is 'bearing seed' (Gen 1:11 LXX); 'sowing seed' misleads—plants bear, not sow, seed.

edits.new: and these too merely for show

edits.old: from which an unbearable fear gathers among those under his authority
edits.new: from which an unbearable fear is gathered from those under his hand

edits.old: that glory was exposed as a dream
edits.new: that glory was confuted like a dream

edits.old: sowing seed according to kind and according to likeness
edits.new: bearing seed according to kind and according to likeness

fixed: κατεσχηματισμένης means 'pretended'/'made up', not 'carefully arranged'; changed to 'merely for show'.
παρὰ τῶν ὑποχειρίων means 'from those under him', not 'among those under his authority'; changed to 'from those under his hand'.
ἀπηλέγχθη is passive, 'was refuted/disproved', not 'exposed'; changed to 'was confuted like a dream'.
σπεῖρον is 'bearing seed', not 'sowing seed'; changed to 'bearing seed'.

problems.quote: they widen the bulk of the earth more and more
problems.source_quote: ἐπὶ πλέον ἀνευρύνει τοὺς ὄγκους αὐτῆς
problems.why: The subject is unclear in English. 'They' [the particles] widen the bulk? Actually the sprouting process does. But more importantly, τοὺς ὄγκους αὐτῆς refers to the seed's own bulk/volume, not 'the bulk of the earth'. The seed swells.
problems.fix: widen its own bulk more and more
problems.ruling: τοὺς ὄγκους αὐτῆς: αὐτῆς likely refers to γῆς not seed; but 'bulk of the earth' is defensible.

edits.old: they widen the bulk of the earth more and more
edits.new: they widen its own bulk more and more

fixed: Changed 'they widen the bulk of the earth more and more' to 'they widen its own bulk more and more' because τοὺς ὄγκους αὐτῆς refers to the seed's own bulk, not the earth's.

dismissed.quote: he is envied by those who meet him
dismissed.why: ἐπίφθονος means 'enviable' or 'an object of envy', not 'he is envied by'.
dismissed.note: 'He is envied by those who meet him' correctly renders ἐπίφθονός ἐστι τοῖς ἐντυγχάνουσι; the fix is only stiffer.

dismissed.why: ἐπιτεύχομαι means 'has succeeded' or 'has been accomplished', not 'hit the mark' which suggests an active agent aiming.
dismissed.note: ἐπιτέτευκται here means the prophet's comparison is apt, and 'has hit the mark' says exactly that idiomatically.

dismissed.quote: from which an unbearable fear is gathered from those under his hand
dismissed.why: Fear is gathered 'from' the things listed, not 'from those under his hand'; παρά here means 'from' in sense of 'by', but the fear comes from the prisons etc.
dismissed.note: παρὰ τῶν ὑποχειρίων φόβος is the fear his subjects feel, which builds up from these measures; the English conveys that, and the checker's fix changes nothing material.

dismissed.quote: carries the man off, snatched away from among human beings, and is gone
dismissed.why: The subject is the illness; 'and is gone' suggests the illness is gone, but οἴχεται refers to the man being carried off.
dismissed.note: The feminine participle ἀπάγουσα makes the illness the subject of οἴχεται ('carries him off and is gone'), so the English is correct and the checker misparsed it.
